chunks: Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who marries off his bondwoman to a free man or to a slave belonging to another people.
He said: “He does not have the right to take her away from him. But if he sells her, and the one who bought her wishes to remove her from her husband, he may do so.”

key_terms.أَنْكَحَ: married off; caused a marriage to be contracted for her
key_terms.يَنْزِعَهَا: to take her away or separate her

ai.seo_question: Can a master separate his bondwoman from the husband he married her to, and does that change after selling her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a bondwoman whom her master marries off to a free man or to another person's slave. The original master cannot separate her from her husband after the marriage, but if ownership passes through sale, the purchaser has the authority to separate her from her husband.
